newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan rupee ends up in kerb, seen stable.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan rupee ends up in kerb, seen stable.

text.p: The Pakistani rupee closed 0.40 up at 41.30 to the dollar in the kerb on Thursday amid heavy selling of the U.S. currency by small investors before the Moslem festival of Eid al-Fitr, dealers said.
"A lot of expatriates coming for Eid holidays are selling dollars, but the dollar is now at a very attractive rate and may not fall further," one dealer said.
The State (central) Bank of Pakistan rate, last changed on October 22, was 40.1200/40.3206 to the dollar.
The premium on foreign exchange bearer certificates closed unchanged at 4.20 percent.
